verses.text: Jesus got into a boat, crossed back over, and came to his own city.
Some people brought him a paralyzed man on a bed. Jesus saw their faith and told the man, “Take heart, son. Your sins are forgiven.”
Some teachers of the Law thought, “This man is disrespecting God.”
Jesus knew what they were thinking. “Why are you cooking up evil in your hearts?”
“Which is easier to say: ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or ‘Get up and walk’?”
“But I’ll show you that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins.” Then he told the paralyzed man, “Get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
The man got up and went home.
When the crowds saw it, they were amazed and praised God for giving this authority to people.
As Jesus walked on, he saw a man named Matthew sitting at the tax booth. “Follow me,” Jesus told him. Matthew got up and followed.
Later, while Jesus was eating at a house, many tax collectors and sinners came and sat down with him and his disciples.
The Pharisees saw this and asked his disciples, “Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
Jesus heard them and answered, “Healthy people don’t need a doctor; sick people do.”
“Go learn what this means: ‘I want mercy, not sacrifice.’ I didn’t come to call the righteous; I came to call sinners to turn back to God.”
Then John’s disciples came and asked, “Why do we and the Pharisees fast so often, but your disciples don’t?”
Jesus answered, “Can wedding guests mourn while the groom is with them? The time will come when the groom is taken away; then they’ll fast.”
“Nobody patches an old garment with unshrunk cloth. The patch will pull away and make the tear even worse.”
“People don’t pour new wine into old wineskins either. The skins would burst, the wine would spill, and the skins would be ruined. They put new wine in fresh wineskins, and both are kept safe.”
While Jesus was saying this, a synagogue leader came, bowed before him, and said, “My daughter has just died. Come lay your hand on her, and she’ll live.”
Jesus got up and followed him, and his disciples came too.
A woman who’d been bleeding for twelve years came up behind him and touched the fringe of his robe.
She was thinking, “If I can just touch his robe, I’ll be made well.”
Jesus turned, saw her, and said, “Take heart, daughter. Your faith has made you well.” The woman was healed that very moment.
Jesus entered the leader’s house and saw the flute players and all the noisy commotion.
He said, “Make room. The girl isn’t dead; she’s sleeping.” They laughed at him.
When the crowd had been sent outside, Jesus went in, took the girl by the hand, and she got up.
Word about this spread all through that region.
As Jesus moved on, two blind men followed him, calling out, “Son of David, have mercy on us!”
When he went into a house, the blind men came to him. Jesus asked, “Do you believe I can do this?” They answered, “Yes, Lord.”
Then he touched their eyes and said, “Let it happen for you according to your faith.”
Their eyes opened. Jesus gave them a strong warning: “Make sure nobody hears about this.”
But they went out and spread the news about him all through that region.
As they were leaving, people brought Jesus a man who couldn’t speak because he was troubled by a demon.
When the demon was driven out, the man spoke. The crowds were amazed: “Nothing like this has ever happened in Israel!”
But the Pharisees said, “He drives out demons by the ruler of demons.”
Jesus traveled through all the towns and villages, teaching in their synagogues, announcing the Kingdom’s Good News, and healing every disease and sickness among the people.
When he saw the crowds, his heart went out to them. They were harassed and scattered, like sheep with no shepherd.
Then he told his disciples, “The harvest is huge, but the workers are few.”
“So ask the Lord of the harvest to send workers out into his harvest.”
